title: Saved shared notes were associated with better puzzle-solving workflows
summary: An audit of 28,568 language-model workflows found that those using a persistent shared document tended to solve more puzzles correctly. Across ten testable puzzles in held-out searches, the median accuracy difference was 13.5 percentage points.
organization: Dartmouth College; Allen Institute for AI

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 workflow search corpus, LightGBM validation design, §V and fixed held-out association Table VI

evidence.tested: The authors mined features of executable workflow variants and evaluated the shared-memory association in held-out search runs. Six of ten comparable test puzzles had intervals strictly above zero.
evidence.unknown: The comparison is observational across searched workflows on selected puzzles. Other choices can correlate with shared memory, and the analysis does not establish a causal advantage on other tasks.
evidence.ai_role: Language models contribute executable workflow variants and mine feature hypotheses; a fitted LightGBM regressor checks predictive features before held-out searches are opened.
